title_candidates: Claude Sonnet 5.5 speeds up everyday work
Try Claude Sonnet 5.5 on a real editing task
summary: Claude Sonnet 5.5 is faster and more efficient than its predecessor, according to Anthropic. A 10-minute editing test shows what that means for ordinary work.

primary_source.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
primary_source.author: Anthropic
key_facts: Anthropic presents Sonnet 5.5 as the everyday-work counterpart to Opus 5.5, aimed at well-defined jobs such as bug fixes and producing polished documents, slides, spreadsheets, and designs.
Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 produces results more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and generally uses fewer tokens for similar work, cutting per-task cost by as much as 30% in its testing.
The announcement keeps standard API prices at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, plus separate prompt-caching rates.

Anthropic reports broad gains over Sonnet 5 in its benchmarks, including a large Terminal-Bench 4.0 jump and near-Opus 5.5 results on two knowledge-work evaluations; these are vendor evaluations rather than independent guarantees.
Users can choose an effort level: lower settings prioritize speed and lower usage, while higher settings spend more time reasoning and checking.
Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 matched or improved on Sonnet 5 across most measures in an approximately 1,850-scenario behavioral audit, while noting that evaluations cannot catch every failure.
Sonnet 5.5 is available in Claude and across Anthropic's developer platforms and major cloud providers.

quote_candidates.text: It’s a clear upgrade over Claude Sonnet 5, runs 30%+ faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work.

supporting_sources.title: Change the model, effort, and thinking settings
key_facts: Users can click the model name beside the send button, choose another model, and open More models when needed.
Sonnet 5.5 supports selectable effort levels; lower settings suit routine work and conserve usage, while higher settings spend more time on difficult tasks.
Thinking cannot be switched off for Sonnet 5.5 in the Claude app.

supporting_sources.title: Why Claude switched models in your conversation with Sonnet 5.5
key_facts: Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 can switch to Sonnet 5 for a narrow group of high-risk requests and displays a notice when this happens.
The related account control is under Settings and Capabilities.

supporting_sources.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
key_facts: Simon Willison highlights Anthropic's speed and per-task cost claims while noting that the model keeps Sonnet 5's API token prices.
His release note points readers to the official Anthropic announcement and benchmark table.

prerequisites: A browser or the Claude mobile app
A free or paid Claude account

steps.instruction: Open [Claude](https://claude.ai), sign in or create an account, and start a new chat. Confirm that the chat box and a model label appear beside the send button.
Select the model label beside Send, choose Claude Sonnet 5.5, and open More models if needed. Confirm that the label now reads Sonnet 5.5 before sending anything.

Paste this invented test: 'Turn these rough notes into a one-page project update with headings Status, Decisions, Risks, and Next actions: launch moved to Friday; homepage review Thursday; owner A checks analytics; risk: mobile images are too large.' Send it and confirm the result has all four headings and preserves every named fact.

Reply: 'Revise this for a non-technical manager, keep it under 150 words, and end with one decision question.' Confirm the revision is shorter, avoids jargon, keeps the facts, and ends with a question.

Check the model label on the answer. It should still say Sonnet 5.5. If Claude shows a model-switch notice, open Settings > Capabilities to review Switch models when a message is flagged; retry only with the harmless sample.

risk_flags: Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 is available on Claude.ai and its plan table lists Sonnet on Free, but free accounts have usage limits and paid plans provide more usage.
Enterprise administrators can hide models or set defaults, so a missing Sonnet 5.5 option may reflect organization policy rather than a failed rollout.
The guide uses invented, non-sensitive notes. Do not ask readers to upload financial records, health data, passwords, or confidential documents.
Sonnet 5.5 can switch to Sonnet 5 for a narrow set of high-risk requests and displays a notice when it does.
Performance, benchmark, and cost-per-task claims come from Anthropic's own evaluation and should be attributed as such.
